items.title: Section: The Chapter on Power Opens — Four Ways Buddhas Save Beings, and Elder Dàochuò's Seven Similes for a Single Name's Power

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩威力？當知略有三種。一者、聖威力。謂佛菩薩得定自在，依定自在，隨其所欲一切事成。
items.en: What is the power of buddhas and bodhisattvas? It should be understood that, in brief, there are three kinds. The first is the power of holiness: buddhas and bodhisattvas attain mastery over concentration, and resting on this mastery, everything they wish for comes to pass.

items.title: The Power of Holiness Completed — A Mind Made Utterly Pliant Through Three Incalculable Eons

items.zh: 心調柔故，善修心故，是名聖威力。
items.en: Because the mind has become pliant, and because the mind has been well cultivated, this is called the power of holiness.

items.title: The Power of the Dharma Opens — Vast Fruit from Supreme Practices

items.zh: 二者、法威力。謂諸勝法有廣大果，有大勝利，是名法威力。
items.en: The second is the power of the Dharma: it is that these supreme practices carry vast fruit and great benefit — this is called the power of the Dharma.

items.title: The Third Power — Innate Power Carried Over From Accumulated Merit, Completing All Three Kinds

items.zh: 此中法者，即是六種波羅蜜多。所謂布施乃至般若。如是諸法有大威力，名法威力。三者、俱生威力。謂佛菩薩先集廣大福德資糧，證得俱生甚希奇法，是名俱生威力。
items.en: The "Dharma" spoken of here refers to the six perfections — giving, and so on up through wisdom. These practices possess vast power; this is called the power of the Dharma. The third is innate power: buddhas and bodhisattvas, having previously gathered vast provisions of merit, thereby attain innate and truly marvellous qualities — this is called innate power.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Power, and the Six Superknowledges That Constitute Miraculous Power

items.zh: 又佛菩薩如是威力品類差別，復有五種。一者、神通威力，二者、法威力，三者、俱生威力，四者、共諸聲聞、獨覺威力，五者、不共聲聞、獨覺威力。
items.en: Moreover, the distinct kinds of power belonging to buddhas and bodhisattvas may further be classified into five: first, the power of miraculous ability; second, the power of the Dharma; third, innate power; fourth, power shared in common with hearers and solitary buddhas; and fifth, power unique to buddhas and bodhisattvas, not shared with hearers or solitary buddhas.

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩神通威力？謂六神通。一者、神境智作證通，二者、隨念宿住智作證通，三者、天耳智作證通，四者、見死生智作證通，五者、知心差別智作證通，六者、漏盡智作證通。是名神通威力。
items.en: What is the miraculous power of buddhas and bodhisattvas? It is the six superknowledges: first, the superknowledge of miraculous ability; second, the superknowledge of recollecting past lives; third, the superknowledge of the divine ear; fourth, the superknowledge of seeing death and rebirth; fifth, the superknowledge of knowing others' minds; and sixth, the superknowledge of the extinction of contaminants. This is called miraculous power.

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩神境智通？

items.title: Miraculous Ability's Two Modes — Transforming What Exists, Conjuring What Did Not

items.zh: 謂佛菩薩神境智通略有二種。一者、能變通，二者、能化通。如是二種品類差別，各有多種。
items.en: The superknowledge of miraculous ability possessed by buddhas and bodhisattvas is, in brief, of two kinds: first, the power of transformation; second, the power of conjuring. Each of these two kinds has, in turn, many further distinct varieties.

items.zh: 云何能變神境智通品類差別？
謂十八變。一者、振動，二者、熾然，三者、流布，四者、示現，五者、轉變，六者、往來，七者、卷，八者、舒，九者、眾像入身，十者、同類往趣，十一者、顯，十二者、隱，十三者、所作自在，十四者、制他神通，十五者、能施辯才，十六者、能施憶念，十七者、能施安樂，十八者、放大光明。
items.en: These are the eighteen transformations: quaking, blazing, pervading, showing, transmuting, coming and going, contracting, expanding, gathering every form into one's own body, going forth in the same form as one's audience, revealing, concealing, freely accomplishing whatever is willed, restraining another's miraculous power, bestowing eloquence, bestowing memory, bestowing ease, and radiating great light.

items.zh: 如是等類，皆名能變神境智通。振

items.title: Section: Quaking Worlds, Blazing Fire and Water, and Light That Fills Every Realm

items.zh: 動者，謂佛菩薩得定自在，心調柔故，善修心故；依定自在，普能振動寺館舍宅、村邑聚落、城郭國土、那落迦世界、傍生世界、祖父世界、人世界、天世界、一四大洲、一千世界、二千世界、三千大千世界、百三千大千世界、千三千大千世界、百千三千大千世界、乃至無量無數三千大千世界皆能振動。是名振動。
items.en: Quaking: buddhas and bodhisattvas, having attained mastery over concentration ... are universally able to make halls and lodges, dwellings, villages, towns, walled cities and countries, the hell realms, the animal realm, the ghost realm, the human realm, and the heavenly realm quake ... up to an immeasurable, uncountable number of great trichiliocosms, all of them able to quake. This is called quaking.

items.zh: 熾然者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，從其身上發猛焰火，於其身下注清冷水；從其身下發猛焰火，於其身上注清冷水。入火界定，舉身洞然，遍諸身分出種種焰，青、黃、赤、白、紅紫、碧綠頗胝迦色。是名熾然。流布者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，流布光明，遍滿一切寺館舍宅，乃至無量無數世界無不充滿，如前振動。是名流布。
items.en: Blazing: ... fierce flames issue from the upper body while cool water pours from the lower body; fierce flames issue from the lower body while cool water pours from the upper body ... this is called blazing. Pervading: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, radiate light pervading every hall, lodge, and dwelling, filling even an immeasurable, uncountable number of worlds without exception ... this is called pervading.

items.title: Section: Showing Every Realm and Every Pure Land — With a Story of a Monk Humbled by His Own Lay Disciple

items.zh: 示現者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，如其所樂，示彼一切諸來會眾沙門、婆羅門、聲聞、菩薩、天、龍、藥叉、健達縛、阿素洛、揭路荼、緊捺洛、牟呼洛伽、人、非人等，令悉現見下諸惡趣、上諸人天。復令現見諸餘佛土，及於其中諸佛菩薩。乃至超過殑伽沙等諸佛國土，種種名聲所表佛土，及彼土中某名如來，悉令現見；亦為宣說彼佛土名，及如來名。
items.en: Showing: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, show to the entire assembly, as they wish, whatever they take delight in ... causing them all to directly see the miserable realms below and the human and heavenly realms above. They further cause them to directly see other buddhas' lands, and the buddhas and bodhisattvas dwelling within them ... causing them all to directly see this, and also proclaiming the name of that buddha-land, and the name of its Tathāgata.

items.zh: 齊彼至此，若復過彼諸佛國土及諸如來，隨其所欲，乃至所欲皆令現見，亦為宣說。是名示現。

items.title: Section: Transmuting the Four Elements — Mind Creates the World It Stands On

items.zh: 轉變者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，若於其地起水勝解，即令成水如實非餘；火、風勝解亦復如是。若於其水起地勝解，即令成地如實非餘；火、風勝解亦復如是。若於其火起地勝解，即令成地如實非餘；水、風勝解亦復如是。若於其風起地勝解，即令成地如實非餘；水、火勝解亦復如是。若於一切起餘勝解，即隨勝解如實非餘。
items.en: Transmuting: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration — if they form the resolute conviction that earth is water, it genuinely becomes water and nothing else; the same holds for resolving it into fire or wind. ... If they form some further resolute conviction regarding all of these — such as that they are empty — it genuinely becomes exactly that and nothing else.

items.zh: 如於大種互相轉變，色、香、味、觸，當知亦爾。

blocks.text: Fascicle 37 contains the chapters on **power** (威力品) and **ripening** (成熟品). Power is what buddhas and bodhisattvas can do, from supernormal transformations to the power of the perfections; ripening is how they bring beings to maturity.

**The power of holiness**: "attaining mastery over concentration, and resting on it, everything they wish for comes to pass", "because the mind has become pliant". Venerable Miào Jìng: the concentration has great majesty. **The power of the Dharma**: "these supreme practices carry vast fruit": the six perfections. **Innate power**: from merit gathered before, they have marvellous qualities by birth.

The five: miraculous, Dharma, innate, shared with hearers, and not shared. Miraculous power is the six superknowledges: psychic power, past lives, divine ear, others' minds, death and rebirth, and the extinction of contaminants.

Psychic power is **transforming** what exists, and **conjuring** what did not. Transformation has eighteen kinds: quaking, blazing, pervading, showing, transmuting, coming and going, contracting, expanding, gathering forms into one's body, appearing in an audience's own form, appearing, disappearing, free accomplishment, restraining others' powers, bestowing eloquence, memory, ease, and radiating light. Venerable Miào Jìng notes how the list was counted.
They make "dwellings, villages, cities, the hells, the animal realm, the ghosts, humans, and gods" quake. Blazing: "fierce flames from the upper body while cool water pours from the lower".
They show the assembly "the miserable realms below and the human and heavenly realms above".

"If they form the resolute conviction that earth is water, it genuinely becomes water." Master Cháng Bǎi: not like stage magic, which cannot be used. The Ru-Yi heading's phrase, "mind creates the world it stands on", links this to the chapter on true meaning: things have no fixed nature apart from mind.

quiz.q: The power of holiness is "mastery over concentration." Why can't a beginner's concentration be called mastery, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: at first the virtues of concentration aren't complete — still less mastery
quiz.why: "The first is the power of holiness: buddhas and bodhisattvas attain mastery over concentration, and resting on this mastery, everything they wish for comes to pass." Venerable Miào Jìng: when one first attains concentration, its virtues aren't yet complete — so of course it can't be called mastery.

quiz.q: "Resting on this mastery, everything they wish for comes to pass." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: the concentration has great masterful power — whatever one wishes succeeds
quiz.why: "Resting on this mastery, everything they wish for comes to pass." Venerable Miào Jìng: because the concentration attained has the majesty of great mastery, whatever one wishes to do, it all succeeds.

quiz.q: "Because the mind is pliant and well cultivated, this is the power of holiness." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "well cultivated"?
options: the buddhas' and bodhisattvas' minds don't cling and aren't defiled
quiz.why: "Because the mind has become pliant, and because the mind has been well cultivated, this is called the power of holiness." Master Cháng Bǎi: buddhas' and bodhisattvas' minds don't cling and aren't defiled — hence "well cultivated."

quiz.q: The "Dharma" here is the six perfections. How long must they be practised, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: before and after non-discriminating wisdom — until buddhahood
quiz.why: "The 'Dharma' spoken of here refers to the six perfections — giving, and so on up through wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: the six perfections must be cultivated before attaining non-discriminating wisdom, and after it too, all the way to buddhahood.

quiz.q: The first superknowledge, "miraculous ability (神境)." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 神境?
options: 神 means inconceivable — an inconceivable domain
quiz.why: "First, the superknowledge of miraculous ability." Venerable Miào Jìng: in 神境, 神 means inconceivable — an inconceivable domain is called 神境.

quiz.q: "The eighteen transformations" — the section headings call "going forth in the same form" ninth and "radiating light" sixteenth. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: eighteen transformations folded into sixteen headings (contract/expand and conceal/reveal merged) — the headings mix the two counts
quiz.why: "These are the eighteen transformations: quaking … and radiating great light." Venerable Miào Jìng: originally eighteen transformations; here they become sixteen headings — contracting and expanding, two items, are merged into one (and likewise concealing and revealing). By the list of eighteen, going forth in the same form is tenth and radiating light eighteenth.

quiz.q: "Resolving earth into water, it genuinely becomes water and nothing else." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "nothing else"?
options: earth truly becomes water — nothing else
quiz.why: "If they form the resolute conviction that earth is water, it genuinely becomes water and nothing else." Venerable Miào Jìng: turning the earth into water, it truly becomes water — not anything else.
